posts.title: Everything I know about writing
posts.description: photo cred: my dad 1. A few years ago, some researchers put ants and humans in a head-to-head battle of wits. The task was to maneuver an awkwardly sized object through a series of obstacles, like this: Humans and ants competed both as individuals and in groups. The humans were forbidden from communicating with one another (I guess to make the playing field more level with the ants?), and they were made to wear sunglasses and masks to prevent any nonverbal signals. The ants were allowed to do whatever they wanted, on account of them being ants. Researchers “incubated” the objects in cat food and rubbed them with tuna to make them “seem like attractive food items to the ants” (I assume humans were spared this step). I have read the paper multiple times and I still don’t really understand why they did any of this, but the videos they made are really cool : I bring this up because watching those videos, I think to myself: that’s exactly what writing is. Submit your preorder receipt and your mailing address here . This is only available to folks with US or UK addresses—apologies to those who live elsewhere! posts.title: Fake it ‘til you make it (and then keep faking it)
posts.description: photo cred: my dad This is the quarterly (really more like trimester-ly) links ‘n’ updates post, a collection of things I’ve been reading and doing for the past few months. (1) FAKE IT ‘TIL YOU MAKE IT (AND THEN KEEP FAKING IT) A few years ago, a blog called Data Colada presented evidence of fraud in several papers by then-Harvard Business School professor Francesca Gino. She was later fired, although she denies wrongdoing and the litigation is ongoing. (For more, see I’m So Sorry for Psychology’s Loss, Whatever It Is .) Now, Data Colada is making similar allegations about pop psych superstar Dan Ariely ( 1 , 2 ). The paper in question is benign enough : it claims to show that when you let students pick their own deadlines, they get worse grades than when you evenly space their deadlines out for them.
